heuristic.applicability: Prefer when the hole is near the demonstrated world workspace but invocation phase is ambiguous: the predecessor may hand off high during descent, near the insertion line, after engagement, or already near stable completion. All object poses and robot state must remain within a plausible reachable, collision-free regime.

handoff.entry_conditions: Peg is closed-grasped and visible; hole, target, peg, TCP, qpos, and qvel are finite. The hole should be near its demonstrated world pose because this model predicts world-frame targets. Entry can be early, during insertion, or late in the stable tail.
handoff.exit_conditions: Only the supplied head-x interval, y/z tolerance, minimum axis alignment, and stable held pose define success. The inferred phase is guidance and never a success substitute.
handoff.failure_signatures: Stage logits conflict with visible geometry; world targets do not follow a moved fixture; descent begins with lateral/axis error; insertion stalls; peg separates from TCP; or IK reports nonconvergence/limits. No class denotes jam recovery.
handoff.overlap_role: The complete assigned segments are trained. The 1380-1500 overlap contains high alignment, descent, insertion-line settling, and initial +x motion, supplying multiple observable phases to both adjacent skills.
handoff.successor_readiness: There is no learned successor. A hold phase should preserve the closed grasp, but the framework evaluates readiness only from unchanged task geometry and stability.

heuristic.limitations: The auxiliary stages are deterministic labels from nominal geometric progress and do not establish contact. They may be wrong for collisions, jams, dropped pegs, or unusual approaches. World-frame absolute actions intentionally retain the demonstrated robot/workspace pattern and are not fixture-displacement invariant; the hole-frame prior covers that shift. Auxiliary supervision supports but does not replace diffusion.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Use this model for uncertain switch timing near the nominal fixture pose. The trainable causal encoder and stage head must be registered, optimized, EMA-saved, and feed the diffusion condition; masked cross-entropy is auxiliary to active action diffusion. Route materially displaced holes to the hole-frame prior and local tracking perturbations to the fresh-TCP residual prior.
heuristic.rationale: A two-frame observation can occur in qualitatively different responsibilities: high descent, insertion-line advancement, or terminal hold. The trajectories show a z-dominant transition from about 0.42 m to 0.10 m, then +x insertion from peg center near -0.31 m to -0.182 m, followed by repeated stabilization targets. A causal phase auxiliary objective forces a learned encoder used by diffusion to preserve those distinctions, while absolute world Cartesian actions retain configuration/workspace regularities that the invariant policies may discard.
heuristic.statement: Causal phase-aware world-target prior: use a registered geometry encoder with an auxiliary approach/insert/stabilize head that conditions the diffusion backbone; diffuse absolute world TCP position, projected 6D rotation, and gripper command.

assignment.subgoal: Keep the peg grasped, complete axis/lateral alignment over the square hole, descend to the insertion line, drive the peg along +x until the supplied head-position and alignment criteria are met, and stabilize.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Reconstruct each demonstrated world TCP command from xyz and projected 6D rotation, solve with shared IK from the matching measured joints, and compare FK position, rotation angle, and preserved gripper scalar to the demonstrated commanded target.

contract.cut_relation: All assigned align-descend-insert-stabilize actions and the complete [1380,1500) overlap are retained. Causal stage labels refine phase representation without changing cuts, success criteria, or future inference inputs.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is an absolute world-frame TCP target: xyz metres, world rotation represented by its first two matrix columns (6D), and native gripper scalar. The decoder projects 6D to SO(3) and invokes panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh measured qpos. Prediction slots are t-1 through t+14; execution uses slots 1 through 8. A learned three-class stage head conditions diffusion but does not alter or script decoded targets.
contract.parameter_semantics: destination_object and held_object select observed hole_pose and peg_pose for geometric progress features. phase_strategy selects the declared causal approach/insert/stabilize classifier; it is intent metadata and never a caller-supplied phase label or actuator value.
